coverageNote: Disk enumeration matched the expected 6 units / 47 files exactly (root unit = 16-venues-studios-spaces/ itself with venues-studios-spaces-index.md, venues-studios-spaces-cx.md, 16.04, 16.07; plus 16.01, 16.02, 16.03, 16.05, 16.06). Read in full: all 6 sub-domain/domain index files, all 6 CX files, and all 16 small/medium leaf features (Behavior + Edge Cases + States + Decisions + Open Questions). For the 15 largest leaf files (16.01.01, 16.01.02, 16.02.01-03, 16.03.01-02, 16.05.01-02, 16.05.06-07, 16.06.01-03, 16.06.06 — 954 KB of the tree's 1.38 MB) I read Decisions and Open Questions verbatim in full, plus full Behavior/Edge/States for 16.01.01 and 16.01.02, plus a programmatic gap-language scan (undefined / unspecified / nobody owns / unowned / not modelled / no mechanism / contradict) across every line of every file, and a programmatic scan of every [PENDING]/[DEFERRED]/[OWNER] marker with its deferral target and every CX-map-row-vs-detail-section pairing. The full Behavior/Edge prose of those 15 largest files was therefore analysed by targeted extraction rather than read verbatim end to end; a contradiction confined to unscanned Behavior prose in those files could have been missed. Every unit received the 3a/3b/3c cycle. This tree is unusually rigorous: the overwhelming majority of gaps are already carried as Open Questions with an explicit owner and a live deferral target, which per the rubric are not findings.

findings.claim: The domain index's Children table records the status of all 7 children as [SURFACE] and asserts 'All nodes `[SURFACE]` — breadth pass only', but every one of the 7 is at a different status on disk. The pipeline key file for this domain therefore misreports the depth state of the entire tree, while each sub-domain index reports its own children correctly.

findings.failure_scenario: A downstream stage (or a human deciding where to spend deepening effort) reads the domain index — the file every downstream workflow is instructed to read first — and concludes no node in domain 16 has been deepened past the breadth pass. In fact 12 leaf features are [DEEP] and 14 are [PARTIAL]. The stage either re-runs deepening on already-deep nodes or treats ratified [DEEP] decisions (e.g. 16.02.02 D-05's field triple, 16.05.06 D-01..D-27) as provisional breadth-pass sketches.

findings.claim: 16.04 states in its Behavior section that it carries the lockout room's monthly price, and states three times over — in the same file's boundary callout, in D-08, and reciprocally in 16.06.07 D-06 — that 16.06.07 owns the price. Both statements are unmarked and cannot both hold for the lockout monthly price.
findings.evidence: 16.04-rehearsal-practice-space-specification.md:70-71 — 'It is handled in **16.06.09**; this feature only carries the flag that a room *is* lockout-capable and its monthly price.' vs 16.04-rehearsal-practice-space-specification.md:55-58 — '> **Boundary, stated once so the two enums cannot overlap: 16.06.07 owns the price and the rate-card term; 16.04 owns the provision posture; 15 owns the items.**' and 16.04:159 D-08 — '15 owns the items; **16.06.07 owns the price and the rate-card term; 16.04 owns the provision posture**'. Reciprocally 16.06.07-rate-cards-inclusions-extras.md:126 D-06 — '**Boundary with the room spec's provision posture, stated once: this feature owns the price and the rate-card term; the room spec owns whether a thing is provided at all.**' 16.04's own Happy Path step 3 also routes price away: 'plus price (16.06.07) and access model' (16.04:78-79).
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the rehearsal room spec puts a `lockout_monthly_price` field on the 16.04 room-spec entity per line 71; a second implementer building the rate card puts the lockout monthly rate on the 16.06.07 rate card per D-06 and the boundary callout. Either the field exists twice and drifts — the exact duplication failure 15.07.03 DT-01 and 16.04 D-08 exist to prevent, one level up — or it exists on neither because each side assumed the other owned it, and the Edge Case copy 'Lockout only — £X/month. Enquire about tenancy.' (16.04:97) has no source for £X.

findings.forcedInvention: The shape and type of the 'comfortable band size' field: one integer, an integer pair (comfortable / tight), or free text — and whether it is filterable.
findings.claim: 16.04's spec-sheet field list types every other field it introduces (a provision-posture enum, an access-model enum, a sale-model enum, a storage enum) but leaves 'comfortable band size' as an un-typed prose sentence whose example carries two numbers while calling it one 'number'. Nothing else in the file or in 16.06.06 (which consumes the spec for filtering) fixes the shape.
findings.evidence: 16.04-rehearsal-practice-space-specification.md:61-62 — '- **Room size + comfortable band size** — square footage and the honest "this holds a 4-piece comfortably, a 6-piece tightly" number.' Compare the typed siblings in the same list: 16.04:51-53 '**Provision posture — typed here, per category** (D-08). A single enum per backline category: `included` · `hire-extra` · `bring-your-own-only` · `none`'; 16.04:59 '**Access model** — `staffed hours` (with a schedule) / `24h fob` / `by arrangement`'; 16.04:65 '**Sale model** — `hourly` / `lockout` / `both`.' No Decision, Edge Case, State or Open Question in 16.04 addresses the band-size field's shape.
findings.failure_scenario: Implementer A models `comfortable_band_size: integer` (=4 for the example room) and a search filter 'fits a 5-piece' excludes the room. Implementer B models `{comfortable: 4, maximum: 6}` and the same filter includes it. Implementer C stores the sentence as free text and the field cannot be filtered at all — defeating the Happy Path's premise that a band 'filters rehearsal rooms' on the four facts the spec exists to publish (16.04:75-76).

findings.claim: 16.01.05's States table says the `permanently closed` state is reached by 'Operator sets, **or corroborated + timeout**'. The same file's Behavior, its Edge Cases row and its ratified D-06 all say the corroboration-plus-timeout path reaches only `possibly closed` and explicitly never `permanently closed`. Neither statement carries a supersession or contested marker.
findings.evidence: 16.01.05-place-status-at-risk-signalling.md:75 — '| Permanently closed | Operator sets, or corroborated + timeout | Read-only historical record; still linked from past gigs |' vs 16.01.05:62 — '**2 corroborating reports from distinct accounts + a 21-day Operator non-response window** flips the record to `possibly closed` (**never to `permanently closed` — that stays Operator-only**)' and 16.01.05:104 D-06 — 'The auto-flip to `possibly closed` uses a provisional **2 distinct-account corroborations + 21-day non-response** threshold, applied only to unclaimed/silent records' and 16.01.05:76 — '| Possibly closed | ≥2 corroborating reports from distinct accounts + 21-day Operator non-response (provisional; unclaimed/silent records only) |'.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the place-status state machine from the States table (the section that is the state machine's specification) wires corroboration + 21-day timeout to `permanently closed`. A trading grassroots venue that two accounts report as dark — the exact griefing vector 16.01.05 D-02 was written to defeat ('a false closure flag on a trading venue is a direct commercial harm', 16.01.05:45-46) — is marked permanently closed, becomes a read-only historical record, loses bookability, and cascades closure to every room's calendar and live reservations per 16.01-place-records-rooms-cx.md:110 CX-04. A second implementer reading D-06 wires it to `possibly closed`, which is merely search-suppressing and reversible. The two systems differ in whether the platform can permanently kill a live venue's listing on two anonymous reports.

findings.claim: 16.01.03 mandates a studio shot list that includes the control room / desk, the patch bay and the mic locker, and specifies no rule about equipment serial numbers being legible in those photos. The domain CX file names this collision with domain 15's serial-withholding policy, states it is 'unowned', and instructs that domain 16 must not let it fall between the domains — but no Open Question, Decision or [PENDING] in 16.01.03 (or anywhere in 16.01) picks it up, so the hazard has no owner and no deferral target.
findings.evidence: 16.01.03-structured-photo-checklist-virtual-tours.md:30 — '- Studio room: live room wide, **control room / desk, patch bay, mic locker**, isolation booths, piano/backline'. The hazard, stated at domain level: venues-studios-spaces-cx.md:276-280 — 'Separately, a **boundary contradiction** surfaces here: 16.01.03's structured photo checklist asks for a control-room photo — a photo of the desk and rack — and serials are **legible in photos**, while 15.07.03 withholds serials unconditionally in text (16.03.02 → 16.01.03). Domain 16 must not let this fall between the domains: the photo requirement needs a serial-obscuring rule or 15's text policy is quietly defeated.' and venues-studios-spaces-cx.md:287 — '3. **Permission intersection**: The photo-upload permission (Operator) collides with 15's serial-withholding policy — **unowned**.' 16.01.03's Open Questions are Q-01 (Operator take-down of unflattering band photos), Q-02 (shot-type validation) and Q-03 (virtual tour hosting) — 16.01.03:110-112 — none of which is this. Its Edge Cases carry a privacy [PENDING] for people/likeness (16.01.03:60) but nothing for equipment identifiers.
findings.failure_scenario: The photo checklist ships as specified. Operators upload the required control-room and mic-locker shots at full resolution; a Neve's serial plate and a mic locker's rack labels are readable. Domain 15's unconditional withholding of serials in text (cited as 15.07.03) is defeated by domain 16's own mandatory shot list, and the composition 16.03.02 Q-01 already worries about ('gear list + address + a live known-empty calendar', 16.03.02:309) is worsened by machine-readable identifiers of the specific items. No implementer is prompted to add downscaling, redaction, or an access gate on these slots, because no requirement in the feature that owns the upload mentions serials at all.

findings.failure_scenario: The release-to-waitlist path is declared three separate times (CX-06 cancellation, CX-11 recurring skip, and CX-02's expired hold, which does have a detail entry) and only one of the three is analysed. Nothing states the ordering or de-duplication when a cancellation and a recurring skip release the same slot, who is offered it first, or whether the released instance inherits the series' terms — so an implementer building backfill must invent the priority rule for two of the three triggers.
